correctness.rationale: The polar-vertex classification follows from the connected tight-cross-edge graph criterion, explicitly proved, and implies the complete signed facet inequalities. Squared facet normals are p-s^2/N and q-t^2/N. Central symmetry rigorously reduces the global insphere optimization to the origin. Antipodal active facets force centers perpendicular to all maximal normals; strict nonactive slack gives the exact converse and affine dimension. Balanced sign vectors span only within-class contrasts for even part size and the additional between-class line for odd part size. The balanced-even endpoint is the minimum of a strictly increasing explicit function of |s|. Exact rational verifier passed 1,462 assertions; no finite census is used for the general proof.

value.rationale: The complete-bipartite symmetric edge polytope is a canonical, widely studied infinite family. The result determines exactly the maximum Euclidean insphere, every touching facet and the affine dimension and defining inequalities of every optimal center; in equal even sizes it gives the entire center segment in radicals. Nonuniqueness changes sharply with parity and balance despite fixed type of facet classification, a structural geometric phenomenon relevant to canonical-center rigidity, not an arbitrary finite calculation or mere renaming.
